title: N4 - do the probabilities mean what they claim
doc_ref: docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul - 'Make the boundary between yes and no unambiguous'
note: Twenty resume snippets with a deliberately crisp question, ten true and ten false, of which roughly six sit on the boundary by construction: a skills list, coursework, a bootcamp, hobby code, open-source work, and a job adjacent to Python rather than in it. Twenty samples cannot establish calibration; they can show a systematic bias if one is large. Every headline number here carries a bootstrap interval for that reason.

used_python_at_work.instructions: Does the resume state that the candidate has used Python at work?

criteria.true: Describes writing or maintaining Python in a paid role
criteria.false: Mentions Python only outside paid work, or not at all

states.state: I spent two years building ETL pipelines in Python at a logistics company.
At my last role I maintained a Django service handling payments.
Part of my job at Acme was writing Python scripts to automate our weekly reporting.
I trained and deployed recommendation models in Python for an e-commerce team.
As an SRE I wrote Python tooling for our deployment pipeline.
As an independent consultant I delivered three client projects in Python during 2023.
I built our test automation framework in Python while working at a fintech.
I was employed as a research engineer and used Python daily for simulations.
My team's stack was Java on the backend with Python for all our data tooling, which I owned.
I taught an introductory Python class at a community college for two semesters.
states.note: Boundary: a paid role in which Python was used, but not as an engineer.

states.state: My experience is in Java and Go. I have not used Python.
Skills: Java, Kotlin, SQL, Python, Docker, Kubernetes.
states.note: Boundary: listed as a skill with no claim of having used it anywhere.

states.state: I took two university courses that used Python for numerical methods.
I completed a twelve-week data science bootcamp taught entirely in Python.
I write Python on weekends for a hobby project that scrapes cycling results.
states.note: Boundary: skilled use, explicitly outside work.

states.state: I am currently learning Python in the evenings and hope to use it professionally.
I worked alongside a Python team as a product manager but did not write code myself.
states.note: Boundary: Python at work, but not the candidate's.

states.state: Fifteen years of embedded C and C++ across automotive suppliers.
I contribute to an open-source Python library in my spare time.
During my internship I worked on a Java codebase; I had learned Python at university.
